Misuse note: Do not translate every 告白 as a love confession. Identify what is disclosed and to whom.

Meaning: mutual crush with neither side aware
Usage note: 両 combines two instances of 片思い: each person believes or behaves as though the love is one-sided, even though the feelings match.
Example 1 (Japanese): 二人とも好きなのに気づいていない両片思いの状態だ。
Example 1 (English): They both have feelings for each other, but neither realizes it.
Example 2 (Japanese): 両片思いが長すぎて、読者のほうがじれったくなる。
Example 2 (English): Their unspoken mutual crush lasts so long that readers get impatient.
Contrast: 片思い: one-sided love / 両思い: mutual love recognized as such
Misuse note: Do not use it once both people have recognized and communicated their feelings; that is simply 両思い.

Usage note: 燃える展開 is not merely exciting. It evokes rising spirit: a comeback, alliance, sacrifice, or challenge that makes the audience want to cheer.
Example 1 (Japanese): かつてのライバルが助けに来る燃える展開だった。
Example 1 (English): It was a thrilling turn when the former rival arrived to help.
Example 2 (Japanese): 劣勢から全員で立ち上がるのは燃える展開だ。
Example 2 (English): Seeing everyone rise together after falling behind is the kind of comeback that gets you fired up.
Contrast: 胸熱展開: emotionally stirring or triumphant development / 神展開: broadly judges a development excellent
Misuse note: Do not translate it literally as a plot that burns. Render the audience's excitement or the rousing turn.

Usage note: Reduplicated 甘々 intensifies 甘い. In romance it means openly tender and low-conflict; in food it can mean extremely sweet.
Example 1 (Japanese): 付き合い始めた二人の甘々な日常が描かれる。
Example 1 (English): The story follows the couple's lovey-dovey daily life after they start dating.
Example 2 (Japanese): 砂糖を入れすぎて、コーヒーが甘々になった。
Example 2 (English): I added too much sugar, and the coffee became extremely sweet.
Contrast: ラブラブ: visibly in love as a couple / いちゃいちゃ: flirt or act physically affectionate, sometimes annoying observers
Misuse note: Do not default to negative 'sickeningly sweet.' The phrase may be enthusiastic praise, and it also has a literal food meaning.

Usage note: さん adds a personable, sometimes TV-host-like warmth to 新婚. Depending on context, it may refer to one newlywed person or the couple as a unit.
Example 1 (Japanese): 隣の部屋に新婚さんが引っ越してきた。
Example 1 (English): A newlywed couple moved into the apartment next door.
Example 2 (Japanese): 二人は新婚さんみたいに仲がいい。
Example 2 (English): Those two get along like newlyweds.
Contrast: 新婚夫婦: explicit newly married couple / 夫婦: married couple without saying how recently
Misuse note: Do not assume people welcome questions about how 'newlywed' they are. The term is friendly but still concerns private relationship status.

Usage note: 痴話 refers to intimate talk between lovers; 痴話喧嘩 is their quarrel. The label often carries an outsider's amused or dismissive judgment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 二人の痴話喧嘩に友人まで巻き込まれた。
Example 1 (English): Even their friends got dragged into the couple's quarrel.
Example 2 (Japanese): ただの痴話喧嘩だと思って、誰も止めに入らなかった。
Example 2 (English): Everyone assumed it was just a lovers' spat, so nobody intervened.
Contrast: 夫婦喧嘩: quarrel between spouses, without necessarily calling it trivial / 口喧嘩: verbal argument between any people
Misuse note: Do not use the term to dismiss threats or violence as a private couple matter. It is appropriate only when the conflict is genuinely minor.

Usage note: In 鬱展開, 鬱 works as fandom shorthand for a deeply depressing sequence of events. The term evaluates the viewer's emotional burden, not a character's diagnosis.
Example 1 (Japanese): 仲間が次々に離れていく鬱展開が続く。
Example 1 (English): The story enters a bleak stretch as the companions leave one after another.
Example 2 (Japanese): 中盤の鬱展開を越えると、少し希望が見えてくる。
Example 2 (English): After the bleak middle arc, the story finally offers some hope.
Contrast: シリアス展開: serious turn that need not be depressing / 胸糞展開: upsetting because it feels cruel, unjust, or disgusting
Misuse note: Do not translate it as 'a depression plot' or use it to diagnose a person. Prefer 'bleak,' 'grim,' or 'depressing' for the narrative effect.

Usage note: The slang prefix 神 means exceptional or god-tier. 神アニメ praises the work as a whole, though speakers may use it jokingly or impulsively.
Example 1 (Japanese): 作画も脚本もすばらしくて、今期の神アニメだと思う。
Example 1 (English): The animation and writing are excellent; for me, it is the standout anime of the season.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最終回まで見て、神アニメという評価に納得した。
Example 2 (English): After watching the finale, I understood why fans called it exceptional.
Contrast: 名作アニメ: acclaimed or enduring masterpiece, less slangy / 覇権アニメ: title perceived to dominate a season's attention or sales
Misuse note: Do not translate 神 literally as religious 'divine.' Also avoid presenting this fan judgment as an objective category.

Usage note: Literally 'second-year middle-school syndrome,' the joke targets behavior associated with early-adolescent self-dramatization. It is now also a deliberate character aesthetic.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼は右目に特別な力があるという厨二病設定を作った。
Example 1 (English): He invented a chūnibyō persona in which his right eye has a special power.
Example 2 (Japanese): 昔書いた必殺技の名前を見ると、中二病だったころを思い出す。
Example 2 (English): Seeing the special-move names I wrote reminds me of my chūnibyō phase.
Contrast: 中二病: standard spelling of the same slang concept / 邪気眼: a subtype centered on pretending to possess a hidden supernatural power
Misuse note: Do not describe genuine delusions or mental illness with this label. It is teasing slang, not clinical vocabulary.

Usage note: 友情パワー makes an abstract bond behave like literal power. Battle stories may depict it as morale, cooperation, or an actual supernatural boost.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最後は仲間の声援を受けた友情パワーで逆転した。
Example 1 (English): In the end, support from the hero's friends inspired a comeback.
Example 2 (Japanese): 友情パワーだけで勝つ結末には賛否が分かれた。
Example 2 (English): Viewers were divided over an ending won solely through the power of friendship.
Contrast: 仲間との絆: the bond itself, with less jokey trope language / ご都合主義: criticism that events work out too conveniently
Misuse note: Do not assume the phrase is always sincere praise. It can sarcastically criticize an unearned victory.

Meaning: embarrassing past; personal history one wants buried
Usage note: 黒歴史 labels a past episode the speaker treats as humiliating, regrettable, or disowned. It can range from playful self-mockery to concealed institutional history.
Example 1 (Japanese): 中学生のころのブログは、今では完全に黒歴史だ。
Example 1 (English): My middle-school blog is now an embarrassing chapter I would rather bury.
Example 2 (Japanese): 昔の服装を黒歴史扱いするのはやめてよ。
Example 2 (English): Stop treating the way I used to dress as some shameful past.
Contrast: 恥ずかしい過去: plain description of an embarrassing past / 消したい記憶: memory one wishes to erase, without the fixed slang label
Misuse note: English 'black history' has unrelated cultural meanings. Translate the intended regret or embarrassment rather than the characters literally.

Meaning: so relatable; a familiar shared experience
Usage note: Repeated ある conveys 'that happens.' As a reaction, あるある enthusiastically confirms recognition; as a noun, it refers to the recurring pattern itself.
Example 1 (Japanese): 締め切り前だけ部屋を掃除したくなるの、あるある。
Example 1 (English): Wanting to clean your room only when a deadline is near—so relatable.
Example 2 (Japanese): 学生あるあるを集めた動画を見た。
Example 2 (English): I watched a video collecting experiences every student knows.
Contrast: わかる: 'I get it/I relate,' responding from personal understanding / ありがち: common or predictable, often with mild criticism
Misuse note: There is no single fixed English noun equivalent. Translate it as 'relatable,' 'common experience,' or the specific recurring situation.

Meaning: relatable comedy bit; joke built on a common experience
Usage note: ネタ means material or a bit; あるあるネタ turns shared recognition into comedy or content. The point is familiarity more than a punch-line structure.
Example 1 (Japanese): コンビニ店員のあるあるネタで会場が笑った。
Example 1 (English): The audience laughed at a routine about situations every convenience-store clerk recognizes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 在宅勤務のあるあるネタを四コマにした。
Example 2 (English): She turned familiar work-from-home situations into a four-panel comic.
Contrast: 内輪ネタ: joke understood mainly by insiders in a particular group / 自虐ネタ: humor based on mocking oneself
Misuse note: Avoid the literal 'there-is-there-is material.' State who recognizes the situation and what kind of content it becomes.

Usage note: 回 counts an installment or episode. A ギャグ回 shifts the usual tone toward jokes, even if it still contains plot information.
Example 1 (Japanese): 重い話が続いたあとに、息抜きのギャグ回が入った。
Example 1 (English): After several heavy episodes, the series inserted a light comedy episode.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今回のギャグ回にも重要な伏線が隠れていた。
Example 2 (English): Even this week's comedy episode hid an important clue.
Contrast: シリアス回: episode dominated by serious drama / 日常回: episode centered on ordinary daily activity, not necessarily jokes
Misuse note: Do not assume a comedy episode is noncanonical or filler. Tone and plot relevance are separate questions.

Usage note: シリアス回 describes tone, not necessarily genre or quality. A series can alternate between comedic and serious episodes.
Example 1 (Japanese): いつものコメディ調から一転して、今回はシリアス回だった。
Example 1 (English): This episode abandoned the usual comic tone for serious drama.
Example 2 (Japanese): シリアス回の直後に総集編が放送された。
Example 2 (English): A recap aired immediately after the serious episode.
Contrast: ギャグ回: comedy-focused episode / 鬱展開: specifically bleak or emotionally punishing developments
Misuse note: Avoid the unnatural English noun 'a seriousness episode.' Use 'serious episode,' 'dramatic installment,' or describe the tonal shift.

Usage note: The suffix 系 means a type or family. 日常系 foregrounds everyday interaction and atmosphere rather than a strongly goal-driven plot.
Example 1 (Japanese): 大きな事件が起きない日常系アニメをよく見る。
Example 1 (English): I often watch slice-of-life anime where no major incident occurs.
Example 2 (Japanese): 日常系に見えて、少しずつ謎が深まっていく作品だ。
Example 2 (English): It looks like a slice-of-life series, but its mystery gradually deepens.
Contrast: 癒し系: soothing effect or type, which may overlap but is not identical / 空気系: loosely connected character interaction and atmosphere, a narrower critical label
Misuse note: Not every story set in daily life belongs to 日常系. The term usually implies that ordinary interaction is the main attraction.

Usage note: ほのぼの suggests quiet warmth and emotional ease rather than excitement. The form ほのぼのとした commonly modifies a scene, story, or atmosphere.
Example 1 (Japanese): 家族の何気ない会話が続く、ほのぼのとした回だった。
Example 1 (English): It was a warm, gentle episode built around the family's everyday conversation.
Example 2 (Japanese): 子どもと犬が遊ぶ姿を見て、ほのぼのした。
Example 2 (English): Watching the child play with the dog gave me a warm feeling.
Contrast: のんびり: leisurely or unhurried / 心温まる: explicitly heartwarming, often more emotionally pointed
Misuse note: Do not force a single adjective such as 'heartwarming' every time. It can describe a gently peaceful tone with little emotional climax.

Usage note: 癒し means emotional relief or comfort; 系 marks a type. 癒し系 emphasizes the recipient's calming impression rather than a literal healing ability.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼女は話し方が穏やかな癒し系キャラだ。
Example 1 (English): She is a soothing character with a gentle way of speaking.
Example 2 (Japanese): 疲れた日は癒し系の動画を見たくなる。
Example 2 (English): On tiring days, I want to watch calming videos.
Contrast: 日常系: narrative genre centered on daily life / 天然系: person perceived as naturally absent-minded or unconventional
Misuse note: Do not translate it as a medical 'healing type.' In most media contexts, 'soothing,' 'comforting,' or 'feel-good' is natural.

Usage note: Literally 'hot blood,' 熱血 evokes emotional fire, justice, perseverance, and loud encouragement. Compounds include 熱血漢 and 熱血教師.
Example 1 (Japanese): 努力と根性を信じる熱血な監督がチームを率いる。
Example 1 (English): A passionately intense coach who believes in effort and grit leads the team.
Example 2 (Japanese): 熱血指導が全員に合うとは限らない。
Example 2 (English): An intense coaching style does not suit everyone.
Contrast: 情熱的: passionate in a broad, neutral sense / 暑苦しい: oppressively intense or overbearing, clearly negative
Misuse note: English 'hot-blooded' can suggest anger or sexuality. Translate the specific passion, idealism, or intensity intended by the context.

Usage note: 王道 is usually positive: familiar elements executed in a satisfying way. It does not necessarily mean stale or unoriginal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 努力・友情・勝利を描く王道の少年漫画だ。
Example 1 (English): It is a classic shōnen manga built around effort, friendship, and victory.
Example 2 (Japanese): 奇抜さより王道を丁寧に描いた作品だ。
Example 2 (English): The work carefully executes a classic formula instead of chasing novelty.
Contrast: 定番: standard favorite or staple / 邪道: unorthodox or improper route, often used playfully as the opposite
Misuse note: Avoid the literal 'royal road' unless explaining the Japanese term. Also do not equate 王道 automatically with cliché; evaluation depends on execution.

Usage note: 原作 is the source work itself, not merely an earlier version. Credits may separately name 原案 for the underlying concept and original ideas.
Example 1 (Japanese): アニメを見たあとで原作の小説を読んだ。
Example 1 (English): After watching the anime, I read the original novel.
Example 2 (Japanese): 映画版では原作の結末が変更されている。
Example 2 (English): The film adaptation changes the ending of the source material.
Contrast: 原案: original concept or story outline / オリジナル作品: work not adapted from existing source material
Misuse note: Do not translate 原作 as 'original story' when discussing a source manga or game; 'source material' is often clearer.

Meaning: anime adaptation; to be adapted into anime
Usage note: The suffix 化 means turning something into a form or state. アニメ化 refers to the process or result of adapting source material as animation.
Example 1 (Japanese): 連載中の漫画が来年アニメ化される。
Example 1 (English): The manga currently being serialized will receive an anime adaptation next year.
Example 2 (Japanese): アニメ化を機に原作の売り上げが伸びた。
Example 2 (English): Sales of the source material rose after the anime adaptation.
Contrast: 実写化: adaptation into live-action film or television / 映像化: broader screen adaptation, whether animated or live action
Misuse note: Do not call every animated version a remake. アニメ化 specifically describes adaptation into animation, often for the first time.

Meaning: live-action adaptation; to adapt as live action
Usage note: 実写 means live-action photography as opposed to animation. 実写化 can adapt manga, anime, novels, or games into film, television, or web productions.
Example 1 (Japanese): その漫画は映画として実写化された。
Example 1 (English): The manga was adapted into a live-action film.
Example 2 (Japanese): 実写化では衣装の再現が難しそうだ。
Example 2 (English): Recreating the costumes may be difficult in live action.
Contrast: アニメ化: adaptation into animation / 映画化: film adaptation, which may be live action or animated
Misuse note: Do not translate it as 'made real.' The term describes the production medium, not whether the story becomes realistic.

Usage note: 作画 literally refers to making the drawings. In anime discussion it can cover character drawings and animated movement; 作画がいい supplies the positive judgment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 戦闘シーンは動きも表情も作画が細かい。
Example 1 (English): The battle scene has detailed animation in both movement and facial expression.
Example 2 (Japanese): 話数ごとに作画監督がクレジットされている。
Example 2 (English): An animation director is credited for each episode.
Contrast: 絵柄: visual drawing style / 演出: direction and presentation of a scene
Misuse note: Do not define 作画 as 'animation quality' alone. Bad, good, limited, and detailed 作画 are all possible; the evaluation comes from context.

Usage note: 声優 is a specialized acting profession, not simply anyone who supplies a voice. Common verbs include 演じる, 担当する, and 声を当てる.
Example 1 (Japanese): 同じ声優が少年役と老人役を演じ分けている。
Example 1 (English): The same voice actor performs both the boy and the old man with distinct voices.
Example 2 (Japanese): 主人公の声優は海外版の吹き替えにも参加した。
Example 2 (English): The protagonist's voice actor also took part in dubbing the overseas version.
Contrast: 俳優: actor, often associated with live-action or stage performance / ナレーター: performer specializing in narration
Misuse note: Do not translate 女性声優 as 'voice actress' automatically unless the context prefers gendered English; 'voice actor' is broadly standard.

Usage note: 主題歌 is the work's designated theme song. It need not literally state the story's theme, and some works have multiple theme songs.
Example 1 (Japanese): 映画の主題歌を主演俳優が歌っている。
Example 1 (English): The film's lead actor sings its theme song.
Example 2 (Japanese): 主題歌の歌詞が物語の結末と重なる。
Example 2 (English): The theme song's lyrics echo the story's ending.
Contrast: オープニング曲: song used in the opening sequence / 挿入歌: song inserted within an episode or scene
Misuse note: Do not assume 主題歌 always means the opening. Check credits or context to see whether it is an opening, ending, or film theme.

Usage note: エンディング曲 identifies placement at the end, not a particular musical style. A series may change the song by season or episode.
Example 1 (Japanese): 静かなエンディング曲が余韻を残した。
Example 1 (English): The quiet ending theme let the episode's mood linger.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最終回だけエンディング曲の二番が流れた。
Example 2 (English): Only the finale used the second verse of the ending theme.
Contrast: オープニング曲: opening theme / 挿入歌: song heard within the main story
Misuse note: Do not confuse the ending song with the background score that happens to play near the end of a scene.

Usage note: 回 counts episodes; 最終回 is the last scheduled installment of the relevant run. A later sequel can still follow.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最終回では十年後の登場人物たちが描かれた。
Example 1 (English): The finale showed the characters ten years later.
Example 2 (Japanese): 来週の最終回は放送時間が三十分延長される。
Example 2 (English): Next week's finale will have an extra thirty minutes.
Contrast: 最終話: final story chapter or episode, often in narrative works / 完結編: concluding installment or arc designed to finish the whole work
Misuse note: Do not infer that the franchise has permanently ended. 最終回 may close only the current season or broadcast run.

Usage note: 次回 means the next installment, and 予告 announces it in advance. Previews may use narration, clips, title cards, or deliberately comic material.
Example 1 (Japanese): 次回予告で新しい敵の姿が映った。
Example 1 (English): A new enemy appeared in the preview for the next episode.
Example 2 (Japanese): 次回予告を見ずに、そのまま再生を止めた。
Example 2 (English): I stopped playback without watching the next-episode preview.
Contrast: 予告編: trailer, especially for a film or work as a whole / 番宣: promotional content for a program
Misuse note: Do not call a full-series trailer 次回予告. The word points specifically to the next installment.

Usage note: A 伏線 is planted in advance so a later event feels prepared or meaningful. It can be dialogue, imagery, behavior, or background information.
Example 1 (Japanese): 第一話の何気ない会話が重要な伏線になっている。
Example 1 (English): A casual conversation in episode one becomes important foreshadowing.
Example 2 (Japanese): 作者は結末につながる伏線を各章に張っていた。
Example 2 (English): The author planted clues leading to the ending in every chapter.
Contrast: ヒント: clue or hint that may directly aid inference / ミスリード: detail designed to steer the audience toward a wrong conclusion
Misuse note: Do not label every unresolved question a 伏線. It may be atmosphere, world-building, a loose end, or simply an error.

Meaning: payoff or resolution of earlier setup
Usage note: 伏線回収 is the payoff, explanation, or fulfillment of foreshadowing. Japanese allows 伏線を回収する and 伏線が回収される.
Example 1 (Japanese): 第一話の台詞が最終回で伏線回収された。
Example 1 (English): A line from the first episode paid off in the finale.
Example 2 (Japanese): 未回収の伏線がいくつか残っている。
Example 2 (English): Several planted threads remain unresolved.
Contrast: 謎解き: solving a mystery / どんでん返し: reversal that changes the audience's understanding
Misuse note: English 'collect the foreshadowing' is unnatural. Use 'pay off,' 'resolve,' or 'tie up' according to the sentence.

Usage note: 神 works as a slang intensifier meaning outstanding. 回 refers to one installment, so 神回 praises a particular episode rather than the series as a whole.
Example 1 (Japanese): 脚本と演出がかみ合った神回だった。
Example 1 (English): It was an exceptional episode in which the writing and direction worked perfectly together.
Example 2 (Japanese): ファンの間では第八話が神回と呼ばれている。
Example 2 (English): Fans often call episode eight the series' standout episode.
Contrast: 神アニメ: praise for an anime as a whole / 当たり回: an especially enjoyable episode, often less emphatic
Misuse note: Do not translate 神 literally in ordinary English or present 神回 as an objective label.

Usage note: 覇権 literally concerns supremacy. 覇権アニメ frames seasonal anime as a competition, but there is no single official criterion for winning.
Example 1 (Japanese): 放送前から覇権アニメ候補として注目されていた。
Example 1 (English): Even before airing, it was seen as a contender to dominate the anime season.
Example 2 (Japanese): 配信再生数だけで覇権アニメを決めるのは難しい。
Example 2 (English): It is hard to name a season's dominant anime from streaming views alone.
Contrast: 人気作: popular work without claiming seasonal dominance / 話題作: much-discussed or anticipated work
Misuse note: Do not define it simply as 'the most popular anime.' Sales, online buzz, streaming, and personal preference are often mixed together.

Usage note: 視聴 combines seeing and listening, and 者 marks a person. The term treats people in their role as audience members.
Example 1 (Japanese): 配信の視聴者から質問を募集した。
Example 1 (English): The stream invited questions from viewers.
Example 2 (Japanese): 視聴者の半数以上がスマートフォンで番組を見ていた。
Example 2 (English): More than half of the viewers watched the program on a smartphone.
Contrast: 観客: audience physically attending a performance or event / 読者: reader of written material
Misuse note: Do not use 視聴者 for readers or game players unless they are specifically watching video content.

Usage note: 考察 in fandom means evidence-based interpretation or theorizing. 考察勢 are the participants known for that activity.
Example 1 (Japanese): 考察勢が背景の記号から黒幕を予想している。
Example 1 (English): Theory-crafting fans are using symbols in the background to predict the mastermind.
Example 2 (Japanese): 考察勢の動画を見てから、第一話を見直した。
Example 2 (English): After watching a fan theory video, I rewatched the first episode.
Contrast: 考察班: playful label for an analysis 'team' / 感想勢: people focused more on reactions and impressions than theories
Misuse note: Do not translate 勢 literally as 'forces.' Use 'fans,' 'crowd,' or 'people who...' according to tone.

Usage note: 一気 means in one burst. 一気見 does not require literally one uninterrupted sitting; the emphasis is rapid consecutive viewing.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末に全十二話を一気見した。
Example 1 (English): I binge-watched all twelve episodes over the weekend.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一気見すると細かい伏線に気づきやすい。
Example 2 (English): Binge-watching makes the small pieces of foreshadowing easier to notice.
Contrast: 見返す: watch again / 流し見: watch with partial attention while doing something else
Misuse note: Do not use the verb without する in formal grammar: 一気見した is the common verbal pattern.

Usage note: The 〜放題 pattern means doing as much as desired. 見放題 usually means unlimited viewing within a plan, not that access is free.
Example 1 (Japanese): この作品は定額プランで見放題になっている。
Example 1 (English): This title is included with the flat-rate streaming plan.
Example 2 (Japanese): 見放題の対象から来月外れるらしい。
Example 2 (English): Apparently it will leave the subscription catalog next month.
Contrast: レンタル: time-limited access purchased per title / 無料配信: distributed without a viewing charge
Misuse note: Do not translate 見放題 as 'free to watch' unless no payment is required. A paid subscription can provide 見放題.

Usage note: 版 means version or edition. 字幕版 contrasts with a version whose spoken dialogue has been replaced by dubbing.
Example 1 (Japanese): 俳優本人の声を聞きたいので字幕版を選んだ。
Example 1 (English): I chose the subtitled version because I wanted to hear the actors' original voices.
Example 2 (Japanese): 字幕版と吹き替え版では上映時間が違う。
Example 2 (English): The subtitled and dubbed versions have different screening times.
Contrast: 吹き替え版: dubbed version / 字幕付き: content with subtitles, including same-language accessibility captions
Misuse note: Do not assume 字幕版 always means accessibility captions. In release listings, it usually means translated subtitles with the original audio.

Usage note: 吹き替え replaces original spoken voices with performances in another language. It is distinct from voice-over narration.
Example 1 (Japanese): 子どもと一緒なので日本語の吹き替え版を見た。
Example 1 (English): Because I was watching with children, I chose the Japanese dub.
Example 2 (Japanese): 吹き替え版では台詞が口の動きに合わせて調整されている。
Example 2 (English): In the dubbed version, the dialogue is adjusted to match the mouth movements.
Contrast: 字幕版: original audio with translated subtitles / ボイスオーバー: another voice layered over audible original speech
Misuse note: Do not call an anime's original Japanese voice track a Japanese 吹き替え. Dubbing replaces an earlier-language performance.

Usage note: ネタ refers here to story content, and ばれ comes from exposure or discovery. The word can name the information, the act, or a warning category.
Example 1 (Japanese): まだ見ていない人がいるから、結末のネタバレはやめよう。
Example 1 (English): Some people have not seen it yet, so let's not spoil the ending.
Example 2 (Japanese): レビューの冒頭に『ネタバレあり』と書いておいた。
Example 2 (English): I put a spoiler warning at the start of the review.
Contrast: あらすじ: plot summary, which may avoid major reveals / 匂わせ: indirect hinting that suggests information without stating it openly
Misuse note: A title, premise, or officially advertised fact is not automatically a spoiler. Audience expectations and timing matter.

Usage note: 班 normally means a small team. In fandom, 考察班 humorously labels the people who collect clues and test interpretations.
Example 1 (Japanese): 考察班が予告映像を一コマずつ確認している。
Example 1 (English): The fan-analysis crowd is checking the trailer frame by frame.
Example 2 (Japanese): この暗号は考察班に任せよう。
Example 2 (English): Let's leave this code to the fandom detectives.
Contrast: 考察勢: the broader cohort of theory-focused fans / 検証班: people checking whether a claim or detail is accurate
Misuse note: Do not assume 考察班 is an official production unit. Translate the playful fan role rather than a literal workplace team.

Usage note: 公式 literally means an official form or formula, but media usage commonly means authorized by the publisher, studio, creator, or other relevant organization.
Example 1 (Japanese): 放送日は公式サイトで確認してください。
Example 1 (English): Check the broadcast date on the official website.
Example 2 (Japanese): その画像は公式が公開したものではない。
Example 2 (English): That image was not released by the official account.
Contrast: 非公式: unofficial / 公認: recognized or approved by an authority, not necessarily produced by it
Misuse note: Do not equate 公式 with objectively true. An official source is authoritative about its own decisions, but translations and announcements can still contain errors.

Kana: せっていしりょうしゅう
Usage note: 設定資料 are reference materials defining a work; 集 means a collection. The book may be official, but the term itself does not guarantee publisher authorization.
Example 1 (Japanese): 設定資料集には衣装の背面図も載っている。
Example 1 (English): The production reference book includes rear views of the costumes.
Example 2 (Japanese): 図書館で昔のアニメの設定資料集を見つけた。
Example 2 (English): I found a production-design reference book for an old anime at the library.
Contrast: 画集: art book focused on finished illustrations / 公式ガイドブック: authorized guide with summaries and reference information
Misuse note: Do not translate every 設定資料集 as 'official art book.' It may focus on technical reference drawings, and official status must be confirmed separately.

Meaning: fictional world and its underlying outlook; setting
Usage note: 世界観 literally means a view of the world. Japanese media usage can include setting, atmosphere, rules, history, and values; English 'worldbuilding' fits only some contexts.
Example 1 (Japanese): 科学と魔法が共存する世界観が魅力だ。
Example 1 (English): The work's world, where science and magic coexist, is compelling.
Example 2 (Japanese): 音楽が作品の独特な世界観を支えている。
Example 2 (English): The music supports the work's distinctive atmosphere and worldview.
Contrast: 設定: specific premise, rule, or assigned detail / 舞台: the place and time where events occur
Misuse note: Do not translate every 世界観 as 'worldbuilding,' which describes a creative process. Sometimes 'world,' 'aesthetic,' 'setting,' or 'worldview' is better.

Usage note: キャラデザ can refer to the design work or resulting designs: silhouette, clothing, colors, facial features, and model choices.
Example 1 (Japanese): 制服のキャラデザは原案よりシンプルになった。
Example 1 (English): The uniform designs were simplified from the original concepts.
Example 2 (Japanese): キャラデザ担当のインタビューを読んだ。
Example 2 (English): I read an interview with the character designer.
Contrast: キャラクター原案: initial character concept designs / 作画: the drawing and animation of characters in actual footage
Misuse note: Do not use キャラデザ as a synonym for animation quality. A design can remain strong even when individual drawings vary.

Usage note: 打ち切る means to stop something at a cutoff point. A 打ち切り may result from sales, scheduling, production trouble, or other decisions.
Example 1 (Japanese): 物語が完結する前に連載が打ち切りになった。
Example 1 (English): The serialization was canceled before the story could reach its conclusion.
Example 2 (Japanese): 視聴率だけが打ち切りの理由とは限らない。
Example 2 (English): Ratings are not necessarily the only reason a program is canceled.
Contrast: 完結: narrative reaches its conclusion / 休載: publication pauses rather than ends
Misuse note: Do not assert that low popularity caused a 打ち切り without evidence. The word describes the early end, not its verified reason.

Usage note: 完結 emphasizes closure as a complete whole. It differs from merely stopping publication or broadcasting.
Example 1 (Japanese): 十年間続いた漫画が今月完結した。
Example 1 (English): The manga concluded this month after a ten-year run.
Example 2 (Japanese): 物語は映画三部作で完結する予定だ。
Example 2 (English): The story is scheduled to conclude with a trilogy of films.
Contrast: 終了: ends or stops, without promising narrative resolution / 打ち切り: is cut short before the expected completion
Misuse note: Do not use 'completed' to imply every mystery was resolved; 完結 states that the work ended as a whole, not that every reader found it satisfying.

Usage note: 連載 means a work appears in successive installments. It can be ongoing, finished, paused, or later collected into volumes.
Example 1 (Japanese): その漫画は月刊誌で連載されている。
Example 1 (English): The manga is serialized in a monthly magazine.
Example 2 (Japanese): ウェブで連載中の小説が書籍化された。
Example 2 (English): The novel currently serialized online was published as a book.
Contrast: 掲載: an item is printed or posted, whether once or repeatedly / 単行本化: installments are collected and published as a book
Misuse note: Do not translate 連載中 simply as 'being written.' It specifically describes ongoing publication in installments.

Usage note: 休載 combines rest with publication. It normally implies that a serialized work is not appearing as scheduled, without declaring it canceled.
Example 1 (Japanese): 作者の体調不良により、今週は休載となった。
Example 1 (English): This week's installment was paused because of the author's poor health.
Example 2 (Japanese): 三か月の休載を経て、連載が再開した。
Example 2 (English): The series resumed after a three-month hiatus.
Contrast: 打ち切り: publication ends prematurely / 連載終了: serialization has ended, whether planned or not
Misuse note: Do not report a work as canceled merely because it is 休載. Check whether a return date or indefinite hiatus has been announced.

Usage note: A 単行本 is a separately published book, often collecting material first serialized elsewhere. It is not inherently a one-volume complete work.
Example 1 (Japanese): 雑誌で読んだ話が単行本に収録された。
Example 1 (English): The chapter I read in the magazine was collected in a book volume.
Example 2 (Japanese): 単行本には描き下ろしの短編が追加されている。
Example 2 (English): The collected volume adds a newly drawn short story.
Contrast: 雑誌: periodical carrying multiple works or installments / 文庫本: small-format paperback edition
Misuse note: Do not translate 単行本 as 'single-volume book.' A manga series can have dozens of 単行本 volumes.

Usage note: 新刊 literally means a newly published book. Xの新刊 often means an author's or series' latest release.
Example 1 (Japanese): 好きな漫画の新刊が来週発売される。
Example 1 (English): The latest volume of my favorite manga comes out next week.
Example 2 (Japanese): 書店の新刊コーナーで面白そうな小説を見つけた。
Example 2 (English): I found an interesting-looking novel in the bookstore's new-release section.
Contrast: 既刊: volumes or titles already published / 新作: new creative work, not necessarily a book
Misuse note: Do not assume 新刊 always means volume one or a brand-new series. It may be the next volume of a long-running work.

Meaning: published volumes to date; existing backlist
Usage note: 既 means already, so 既刊 contrasts released books with forthcoming ones. It may refer to one author's backlist or a series' existing volumes.
Example 1 (Japanese): 休みに入る前に既刊を全巻そろえた。
Example 1 (English): Before the holiday, I bought every volume published so far.
Example 2 (Japanese): このシリーズは既刊八巻で、九巻は秋に出る。
Example 2 (English): The series has eight published volumes, and volume nine arrives in autumn.
Contrast: 新刊: newly published or latest book / 未刊: not yet published
Misuse note: Do not translate 既刊 as 'old books.' Recently released volumes are still 既刊 once published.

Meaning: buying a book for its cover
Usage note: The productive pattern X買い means buying because of X. 表紙買い makes cover art, typography, or design the deciding signal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 書店で表紙にひかれて表紙買いした。
Example 1 (English): The cover caught my eye at the bookstore, so I bought the book on that basis.
Example 2 (Japanese): 表紙買いだったけど、内容も好みに合った。
Example 2 (English): I bought it for the cover, but the story suited my tastes too.
Contrast: 作者買い: purchase based on the author / ジャケ買い: buy music or other media for its jacket or package art
Misuse note: Avoid the literal 'cover buying.' In English, explain that the cover drove the purchase.

Meaning: buying a work because of its author
Usage note: 作者買い means choosing a new title because its author made it, often without needing reviews or a detailed synopsis.
Example 1 (Japanese): あの作家の小説は内容を確認せずに作者買いする。
Example 1 (English): I buy that writer's novels on the strength of the author's name alone.
Example 2 (Japanese): 作者買いした新刊が、いつもの作風と全く違って驚いた。
Example 2 (English): I bought the new book because of the author and was surprised by how different it was from their usual style.
Contrast: 表紙買い: purchase driven by cover design / 指名買い: deliberately buy a specified brand, creator, or product
Misuse note: The term describes purchase motivation, not ownership of the author. Translate the reason naturally.

Usage note: In the party sense, 打ち上げ is a gathering after work concludes or reaches a milestone. The object and verb distinguish it from a physical launch.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最終話の収録後にスタッフが打ち上げを開いた。
Example 1 (English): The staff held a wrap party after recording the final episode.
Example 2 (Japanese): 花火の打ち上げは午後八時から始まる。
Example 2 (English): The fireworks launch begins at eight in the evening.
Contrast: 飲み会: drinking party without a completion requirement / 打ち入り: kickoff gathering before a major project or production
Misuse note: Do not translate every 打ち上げ as 'wrap party.' Rockets, fireworks, and project celebrations use the same noun in different senses.

Meaning: editor assigned to a creator; editor in charge
Usage note: 担当 means being in charge, and 編集 identifies the editorial role. The editor may coordinate deadlines, give story feedback, and connect the creator with the publisher.
Example 1 (Japanese): 漫画家は新しい担当編集と次回作を相談した。
Example 1 (English): The manga artist discussed the next project with the newly assigned editor.
Example 2 (Japanese): 担当編集からネームの修正案が届いた。
Example 2 (English): The assigned editor sent suggestions for revising the manga storyboard.
Contrast: 編集長: editor in chief overseeing an editorial department or publication / 担当者: person in charge in any field
Misuse note: Do not assume 担当編集 is the sole creative author or merely a proofreader. Responsibilities vary by publisher and work.

Usage note: As a noun, 読み切り is a complete standalone piece. It derives from 読み切る, to read through or finish reading, but the publishing term has a fixed sense.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新人賞を取った読み切りが雑誌に掲載された。
Example 1 (English): The award-winning one-shot was published in the magazine.
Example 2 (Japanese): 連載版では読み切りの設定が一部変更された。
Example 2 (English): The serialized version changed some of the one-shot's premises.
Contrast: 連載: serialization across multiple installments / 短編: short work, which may be published alone or within a collection
Misuse note: Do not translate it as 'reading to the end.' Distinguish the noun label 読み切り from the verb 読み切る.

Usage note: 番外 means outside the regular numbering or main sequence. 番外編 adds material beside the central story rather than necessarily continuing it.
Example 1 (Japanese): 番外編では脇役たちの休日が描かれる。
Example 1 (English): The side story follows the supporting characters on their day off.
Example 2 (Japanese): 単行本の巻末に番外編が収録されている。
Example 2 (English): A bonus story is included at the end of the collected volume.
Contrast: 外伝: spin-off or supplementary tale, often larger and more independent / 特別編: special installment created for a particular occasion or format
Misuse note: Do not assume 番外編 is noncanonical or disposable filler. Its relationship to continuity depends on the work.

Usage note: 総集編 gathers selected prior content into one edition. It may add narration or new footage, but compilation remains the main structure.
Example 1 (Japanese): 今週はこれまでの戦いを振り返る総集編だった。
Example 1 (English): This week's episode was a recap of the battles so far.
Example 2 (Japanese): 劇場版はテレビシリーズ前半の総集編になっている。
Example 2 (English): The theatrical film compiles the first half of the television series.
Contrast: 再放送: rebroadcast of an earlier episode as-is / ダイジェスト: condensed highlights or summary
Misuse note: Do not call every 総集編 a 'recap episode.' In film or print, 'compilation film' or 'collected edition' may fit better.

Usage note: シリーズ is flexible in Japanese. 新シリーズ says a new series begins but does not define its continuity or production format.
Example 1 (Japanese): 同じ世界を舞台にした新シリーズが始まる。
Example 1 (English): A new series set in the same world is beginning.
Example 2 (Japanese): 新シリーズは主人公も時代も一新される。
Example 2 (English): The new series changes both the protagonist and the time period.
Contrast: 新シーズン: new season of an existing series / 続編: sequel continuing an earlier work
Misuse note: Do not translate 新シリーズ automatically as 'new season.' Confirm whether it is a sequel, reboot, spin-off, or separate line.

Meaning: favorite person, character, team, or work one supports
Usage note: 推し derives from 推す, to recommend or back. As a noun it means the target a fan actively favors, often with an element of support beyond simple liking.
Example 1 (Japanese): この作品では無口な脇役が私の推しだ。
Example 1 (English): My favorite in this series is the quiet supporting character.
Example 2 (Japanese): 推しが新曲のセンターに選ばれた。
Example 2 (English): My favorite member was chosen as the center for the new song.
Contrast: お気に入り: a favorite, with less fandom or support implication / 担当: one's favored idol or member in some specific fandom traditions
Misuse note: Do not translate every 推し as 'crush.' Fans can have multiple 推し and may support them for performance, design, personality, or story role.

Meaning: fan activities supporting and enjoying one's favorite
Usage note: 推し活 combines 推し with 活動. It packages many forms of support and enjoyment as an ongoing lifestyle activity.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末は友達と推し活でコラボカフェに行く。
Example 1 (English): This weekend, I'm going to a collaboration café with friends as part of our fan activities.
Example 2 (Japanese): 無理のない予算で推し活を続けたい。
Example 2 (English): I want to keep supporting my favorite without exceeding my budget.
Contrast: オタ活: fan or otaku activities more broadly / ファン活動: neutral general term for fan activity
Misuse note: Do not define 推し活 only as buying merchandise. Noncommercial participation and personal enjoyment also count.

Meaning: fall deep into a fandom or hobby
Usage note: The image is of stepping into a deep swamp and being unable to get out. X沼 means the absorbing world surrounding X.
Example 1 (Japanese): 一話だけ見るつもりが、すっかり作品の沼にはまった。
Example 1 (English): I meant to watch one episode and ended up completely absorbed in the series.
Example 2 (Japanese): 友達に勧められて、カメラ沼にはまった。
Example 2 (English): A friend's recommendation sent me deep into the camera hobby.
Contrast: 夢中になる: become engrossed, neutral and broadly usable / ハマる: get hooked on something, without the same depth metaphor
Misuse note: Avoid the literal English 'fall into a swamp' unless explaining the metaphor. The phrase usually expresses enthusiastic absorption, not actual distress.

Meaning: enthusiastically recruit someone into a fandom; recommend
Usage note: Fandom 布教する means actively introducing and promoting a work, performer, or hobby in hopes that others become fans.
Example 1 (Japanese): 友達にこの漫画を布教して、全巻貸した。
Example 1 (English): I tried to get my friend into the manga and lent them every volume.
Example 2 (Japanese): 初心者向けの曲をまとめて、バンドを布教している。
Example 2 (English): I made a beginner-friendly playlist to introduce people to the band.
Contrast: 勧める: recommend, neutral and broadly appropriate / 宣伝する: advertise or publicize, often to a wider audience
Misuse note: Do not use the fandom joke in serious religious contexts, and do not translate it as literal evangelism when a simple recommendation is meant.

Meaning: visiting real locations associated with a work
Usage note: Fandom metaphorically treats filming or model locations as 聖地, sacred sites. Visits may include photography, local shops, and comparison with scenes.
Example 1 (Japanese): アニメの舞台になった町を聖地巡礼した。
Example 1 (English): I visited the town that served as the anime's setting.
Example 2 (Japanese): 聖地巡礼では住民の迷惑にならないように撮影した。
Example 2 (English): While visiting the anime locations, we took photos without disturbing residents.
Contrast: ロケ地巡り: visiting filming locations, without the sacred-site fandom metaphor / 巡礼: pilgrimage or a circuit of significant sites more broadly
Misuse note: Respect access rules and local residents. A work's association with a place does not grant fans permission to enter private property.

Usage note: 二次創作 literally means secondary creation derived from an earlier work. It is broader than fan fiction and does not itself state commercial status or legality.
Example 1 (Japanese): 好きな作品の二次創作イラストを投稿した。
Example 1 (English): I posted fan art based on a series I like.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式の二次創作ガイドラインを読んでから公開した。
Example 2 (English): I read the official derivative-work guidelines before publishing it.
Contrast: 一次創作: original creation not derived from another work / 公式作品: work created or authorized by the rights holder
Misuse note: Do not assume all 二次創作 is automatically licensed, noncommercial, or legally permitted. Check the relevant rights and guidelines.

Usage note: 同人誌 is a publication made by an individual or circle outside mainstream commercial publishing. Manga, fiction, essays, criticism, and research all occur.
Example 1 (Japanese): イベントで創作漫画の同人誌を頒布した。
Example 1 (English): I distributed a self-published original comic at the event.
Example 2 (Japanese): 評論系の同人誌を専門に扱う店もある。
Example 2 (English): Some shops specialize in independently published criticism and research.
Contrast: 商業誌: commercially published magazine or book / 二次創作: derivative creation in any medium, not necessarily a printed dōjinshi
Misuse note: Do not define 同人誌 as pornographic fan comics. It can be all-ages, original, academic, or prose, and the term refers to publication context.

Usage note: コスプレ is shortened from costume play. It includes making or wearing costumes, makeup, photography, and performance to varying degrees.
Example 1 (Japanese): イベントでゲームの主人公をコスプレした。
Example 1 (English): I cosplayed as the game's protagonist at the event.
Example 2 (Japanese): 衣装は自作だが、コスプレ会場でしか着ない。
Example 2 (English): I made the costume myself, but I only wear it at cosplay venues.
Contrast: 仮装: dressing up or wearing a disguise more broadly / 着ぐるみ: full-body character suit or mascot costume
Misuse note: Do not photograph or post cosplayers without consent. Wearing a costume does not waive ordinary privacy boundaries.

Meaning: ita bag; display bag covered with fan merchandise
Usage note: 痛 is playful slang suggesting an excessive or conspicuous display, related to 痛車. The bag is decorated densely with badges, charms, or cards.
Example 1 (Japanese): 推しの缶バッジを並べて痛バッグを作った。
Example 1 (English): I made an ita bag by arranging pin badges of my favorite character.
Example 2 (Japanese): 雨の日は痛バッグにカバーをかけている。
Example 2 (English): I put a cover over my ita bag on rainy days.
Contrast: 痛車: vehicle decorated prominently with character images / 推しバッグ: broader bag used to carry or display favorite-related items
Misuse note: Do not translate it literally as 'painful bag.' Use established 'ita bag' for informed audiences or explain the display style.

Usage note: 缶 refers to the thin metal construction, and バッジ to the wearable item. Character art is printed on the front and a pin is attached behind.
Example 1 (Japanese): 入場特典で丸い缶バッジをもらった。
Example 1 (English): I received a round pin-back button as an admission bonus.
Example 2 (Japanese): 缶バッジの裏がさびないように保管する。
Example 2 (English): I store the pin-back badges so the metal backs do not rust.
Contrast: ピンバッジ: usually a small enamel or molded lapel pin / アクリルバッジ: badge made primarily from acrylic
Misuse note: Do not translate 缶 as a can-shaped object. The item is a flat button or badge made with a metal shell.

Usage note: An アクリルスタンド is a flat printed acrylic piece slotted into a base. It is display merchandise rather than a sculpted figure.
Example 1 (Japanese): 机に推しのアクリルスタンドを飾っている。
Example 1 (English): I display an acrylic standee of my favorite character on my desk.
Example 2 (Japanese): 旅行先でアクスタと風景を一緒に撮った。
Example 2 (English): I photographed the acrylic standee with the scenery on my trip.
Contrast: アクリルキーホルダー: acrylic charm with keychain hardware / フィギュア: three-dimensional figure or statue
Misuse note: Do not call it an acrylic 'stand' alone in English if that suggests only the base; 'standee' identifies the displayed character piece.

Usage note: Although borrowed from English 'goods,' Japanese グッズ often means merchandise tied to a brand, performer, event, or character.
Example 1 (Japanese): 会場限定のグッズを売店で買った。
Example 1 (English): I bought venue-exclusive merchandise at the shop.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式グッズの一覧が公開された。
Example 2 (English): The official merchandise lineup was announced.
Contrast: 商品: product or item for sale in general / 特典: bonus item or benefit supplied under particular conditions
Misuse note: English 'goods' can sound legalistic or generic. Translate fan-related グッズ as 'merchandise' or the specific product type.

Usage note: 限定 only says availability is restricted. It does not automatically mean the item is rare, numbered, or permanently unavailable later.
Example 1 (Japanese): 限定グッズは一人二点まで購入できる。
Example 1 (English): Each person may buy up to two of the limited-edition items.
Example 2 (Japanese): 通販でも買えるので、会場限定グッズではなかった。
Example 2 (English): It was also available online, so it was not venue-exclusive merchandise.
Contrast: 先行販売: sold early before wider release / 特典グッズ: bonus merchandise tied to a purchase or campaign
Misuse note: Do not call an item 'limited edition' without checking what is limited. It may be limited only by sales channel or period.

Meaning: physical disc release; DVD or Blu-ray
Usage note: The physical shape gives the slang meaning. 円盤 often appears in discussions of sales, bonuses, box sets, and home-video corrections.
Example 1 (Japanese): 配信で見た作品の円盤も予約した。
Example 1 (English): I also preordered the series on disc after watching it online.
Example 2 (Japanese): 円盤には放送版で省かれた場面が追加されている。
Example 2 (English): The disc release adds a scene omitted from the broadcast version.
Contrast: 配信版: streamed or digitally distributed version / Blu-ray: specific high-definition disc format
Misuse note: Do not translate fandom 円盤 as a generic 'disk' without context. It usually means a commercial DVD or Blu-ray package.

Usage note: 配信 literally distributes content to recipients. ライブ配信 specifies live streaming; 動画配信 can include on-demand video.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最終話はテレビ放送の直後に配信される。
Example 1 (English): The final episode will stream immediately after the television broadcast.
Example 2 (Japanese): イベントの様子を公式チャンネルでライブ配信した。
Example 2 (English): The event was livestreamed on the official channel.
Contrast: 放送: broadcast through television or radio systems / 配布: distribute files or physical materials to recipients
Misuse note: Do not translate every 配信 as live streaming. Check whether the content is live, on demand, downloadable, or simply digitally released.

Usage note: 公式グッズ is produced, sold, or licensed by the relevant official organization. It may still be manufactured by a partner company.
Example 1 (Japanese): ロゴ入りの公式グッズをオンラインストアで注文した。
Example 1 (English): I ordered official logo merchandise from the online store.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式グッズには著作権表示が印刷されていた。
Example 2 (English): The official merchandise carried a copyright notice.
Contrast: 非公式グッズ: unauthorized or unofficial merchandise / 同人グッズ: independently made dōjin merchandise, which may follow fan-work guidelines
Misuse note: Do not infer official status merely from professional packaging or marketplace claims. Check the rights holder and authorized sales channel.

Usage note: The suffix 組 groups people by route or experience. 原作組 contrasts those who know the source with anime-first or live-action-only viewers.
Example 1 (Japanese): 原作組は登場人物の正体をすでに知っている。
Example 1 (English): People familiar with the source material already know the character's identity.
Example 2 (Japanese): 原作組もネタバレには気をつけている。
Example 2 (English): Source readers are being careful not to spoil anything either.
Contrast: アニメ組: viewers following through the anime adaptation / 初見勢: people experiencing the story for the first time
Misuse note: Do not translate 組 as a formal organization, and do not assume every 原作組 knows all later plot developments.

Usage note: 組 groups people by viewing route. アニメ組 generally contrasts with 原作組 rather than claiming the person watches no other media.
Example 1 (Japanese): 私はアニメ組なので、原作の先の展開は知らない。
Example 1 (English): I only follow the anime, so I do not know what happens later in the source material.
Example 2 (Japanese): アニメ組にも分かるように補足説明が入った。
Example 2 (English): Extra explanation was added so anime-only viewers could follow.
Contrast: 原作組: audience familiar with the source work / アニメ勢: similar informal label for anime-side viewers
Misuse note: Do not translate it as an official 'anime team.' It is an informal audience category and may mean anime-first rather than permanently anime-only.

Meaning: initial sales of the disc release
Usage note: 初動 means initial movement or early performance. With 円盤, it refers to early DVD/Blu-ray sales, not lifetime units or streaming reach.
Example 1 (Japanese): 円盤の初動だけで作品の成功は判断できない。
Example 1 (English): Initial disc sales alone cannot determine whether a series succeeded.
Example 2 (Japanese): 特典イベントの有無で円盤の初動が変わることもある。
Example 2 (English): An event bonus can affect a disc release's first-week sales.
Contrast: 累計売上: cumulative sales over time / 配信再生数: number of streaming plays
Misuse note: Always identify the tracker and period when citing a number. 初動 is not a universal fixed metric and excludes later sales.

Usage note: 劇場 means theater, and 版 marks a version or edition. The term identifies theatrical release format, not the film's relationship to continuity.
Example 1 (Japanese): 人気エピソードが新作映像を加えて劇場版になった。
Example 1 (English): The popular arc became a theatrical film with newly produced footage.
Example 2 (Japanese): 劇場版は来春から全国で公開される。
Example 2 (English): The theatrical film opens nationwide next spring.
Contrast: テレビ版: television version / 実写版: live-action version
Misuse note: Do not assume 劇場版 is a remake or compilation. Check whether it is new, continued, retold, or collected material.

Usage note: Often explained as イケてるメンズ, イケメン primarily means a handsome or attractive man. Figurative uses can praise behavior as cool or considerate.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新しい店員がイケメンだと話題になっている。
Example 1 (English): People are talking about how handsome the new staff member is.
Example 2 (Japanese): 重い荷物を黙って持ってくれるなんて、行動までイケメンだ。
Example 2 (English): Quietly carrying the heavy bags for us—that was a genuinely classy move.
Contrast: 美男子: handsome man, more literary or formal / かっこいい: cool or attractive, usable for people, actions, and things
Misuse note: Do not treat it as a neutral demographic label. It evaluates appearance, and applying it publicly can objectify the person.

Usage note: かわいい系 groups features associated with cuteness—soft colors, rounded forms, gentle presentation—without saying every item is literally cute.
Example 1 (Japanese): このブランドは淡い色のかわいい系の服が多い。
Example 1 (English): This brand carries many clothes in a soft, cute style.
Example 2 (Japanese): 彼女はかわいい系というより、落ち着いたきれい系だ。
Example 2 (English): Her style is more calmly elegant than cute.
Contrast: きれい系: elegant or beautiful type / かっこいい系: cool or sharp style
Misuse note: Do not use the label as an objective judgment about someone's identity. It is a loose style category and may not match self-perception.

Usage note: クールキャラ usually speaks and reacts with restraint. The type may be aloof, competent, dryly funny, or secretly caring.
Example 1 (Japanese): 感情をあまり表に出さないクールキャラだ。
Example 1 (English): He is a cool, composed character who rarely shows emotion.
Example 2 (Japanese): 普段はクールキャラなのに、猫の前では表情が変わる。
Example 2 (English): She is usually the cool, reserved type, but her expression changes around cats.
Contrast: クーデレ: cool exterior paired with a hidden affectionate side / 無口キャラ: character defined specifically by speaking little
Misuse note: Do not equate クール with emotionally cold or cruel. It can be positive praise for composure and style.

Usage note: A pun on 婦女子, 腐女子 uses 腐, 'rotten,' as self-deprecating fandom language. It does not mean a female fan of all anime or manga.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼女は自分を腐女子だと公言している。
Example 1 (English): She openly identifies herself as a fan of boys' love.
Example 2 (Japanese): 腐女子向けと決めつけず、作品の対象読者を確認しよう。
Example 2 (English): Do not assume a work targets BL fans; check its intended audience.
Contrast: 腐男子: male fan of boys' love / オタク女子: woman deeply interested in a hobby, not specifically BL
Misuse note: Do not call someone 腐女子 merely because she likes male characters. The label concerns BL interest and should not be assigned without consent.

Usage note: オタク can mean a devoted hobbyist broadly, not only an anime fan. English 'otaku' is often narrower and more Japan-media-specific.
Example 1 (Japanese): 兄は鉄道オタクで、全国の路線に詳しい。
Example 1 (English): My brother is a railway enthusiast who knows routes all across Japan.
Example 2 (Japanese): 自分ではオタクというほど詳しくないと思っている。
Example 2 (English): I do not think I know enough to call myself an otaku.
Contrast: マニア: enthusiast or collector with specialized interest / ファン: supporter or admirer, without implying the same depth
Misuse note: Do not assume the Japanese word always carries the same identity or stigma as English 'geek,' 'nerd,' or imported 'otaku.' Context matters.

Usage note: Short for 陰気なキャラ. The label bundles perceived quietness, low social status, appearance, and group belonging rather than describing one stable trait.
Example 1 (Japanese): 自分を陰キャと決めつけて、人付き合いを避けていた。
Example 1 (English): He labeled himself an outsider and avoided socializing.
Example 2 (Japanese): 静かな人を全員陰キャ扱いするのは失礼だ。
Example 2 (English): It is rude to label every quiet person as socially inept.
Contrast: 内向的: introverted, neutral descriptive term / ぼっち: someone alone or without companions in a situation
Misuse note: Do not teach 陰キャ as a neutral synonym for 'introvert.' It is a reductive social label and may function as an insult.

Usage note: Short for 陽気なキャラ. The label describes perceived social style and status, not a psychological diagnosis or fixed identity.
Example 1 (Japanese): クラスの陽キャたちが文化祭を盛り上げている。
Example 1 (English): The class's outgoing social crowd is energizing the school festival.
Example 2 (Japanese): 陽キャに見えても、大人数の集まりが苦手な人はいる。
Example 2 (English): Some people look highly outgoing but still dislike large gatherings.
Contrast: 社交的: sociable, neutral descriptive word / リア充: person whose offline life appears fulfilling, a different axis
Misuse note: Do not use 陽キャ and 陰キャ as objective personality tests. They are peer-group labels that flatten individual differences.

Usage note: 隠れ means hidden. Unlike 陰キャ, this label concerns disclosure of a hobby, not sociability or personality.
Example 1 (Japanese): 職場では趣味を話していない隠れオタクだ。
Example 1 (English): I keep my fandom interests private at work.
Example 2 (Japanese): 実は同僚も隠れオタクで、同じ作品が好きだった。
Example 2 (English): It turned out my coworker was a private fan too, and we liked the same series.
Contrast: オープンオタク: person open about their otaku interests / 陰キャ: derogatory social-character label, unrelated to whether hobbies are disclosed
Misuse note: Do not infer shame or dishonesty. Keeping a hobby private can be an ordinary boundary, and 隠キャ is not the correct spelling for this idea.

Meaning: person whose offline life seems fulfilling
Usage note: Short for リアルが充実している, meaning one's 'real' or offline life is fulfilled. The category is based on outward perception and contrast with online life.
Example 1 (Japanese): 週末は友達と旅行なんて、リア充っぽい。
Example 1 (English): Traveling with friends every weekend—that looks like a pretty full social life.
Example 2 (Japanese): 恋人がいなくても、仕事と趣味が充実したリア充はいる。
Example 2 (English): A person can have a fulfilling offline life through work and hobbies without a partner.
Contrast: 陽キャ: outgoing social-character label / 非リア: person self-described as lacking a fulfilling offline or romantic life
Misuse note: Do not define リア充 as simply 'someone in a relationship.' It is broader, subjective, and often used with envy or sarcasm.

Usage note: Probably shortened from 独りぼっち. It can describe a temporary situation or an ongoing social position, with tone ranging from humorous to painful.
Example 1 (Japanese): 昼休みはいつも一人で、クラスではぼっちだった。
Example 1 (English): I always spent lunch alone and had no group in the class.
Example 2 (Japanese): 今日は友達が休みだから、ぼっちで昼を食べる。
Example 2 (English): My friend is absent today, so I'm eating lunch alone.
Contrast: 一人: one person or alone, neutral / 孤独: loneliness or isolation as an emotional/abstract state
Misuse note: Do not assume a person alone is lonely or socially deficient. Use neutral 一人 when no self-deprecating or mocking tone is intended.

Usage note: The productive suffix 枠 means a category or allotted position. 友達枠 says a character is framed as a friend rather than the main romantic option.
Example 1 (Japanese): 恋愛ものでは、主人公を支える友達枠のキャラが好きだ。
Example 1 (English): In romance stories, I like the supportive character in the platonic-friend role.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最初は友達枠だった人物が、後半で恋愛相手になる。
Example 2 (English): A character who began in the friend role becomes a love interest later.
Contrast: 恋愛枠: character positioned as a romantic possibility / 親友ポジション: best-friend narrative position
Misuse note: Do not equate the term mechanically with English 'friend zone,' which often emphasizes rejection and entitlement.

Meaning: foil or secondary suitor used to advance the main romance
Usage note: The original equestrian term referred to a stallion used to stimulate another horse. In stories, the 当て馬 is usually not the final romantic choice.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼は主人公の気持ちを自覚させる当て馬として登場する。
Example 1 (English): He enters as a secondary suitor whose presence makes the protagonist recognize her feelings.
Example 2 (Japanese): 当て馬だと思われていたキャラが最後に選ばれた。
Example 2 (English): The character everyone assumed was only the secondary suitor was chosen in the end.
Contrast: 恋敵: romantic rival, who may still have a genuine chance / かませ犬: character used to demonstrate another's strength by losing
Misuse note: Avoid calling a real person an 当て馬. It reduces them to a tool in someone else's relationship and carries a dehumanizing history.

Meaning: go viral; suddenly attract widespread attention
Usage note: Borrowed from English 'buzz,' バズる is a Japanese verb. Posts, phrases, products, and people can become widely discussed.
Example 1 (Japanese): 短い感想動画が一晩でバズった。
Example 1 (English): The short reaction video went viral overnight.
Example 2 (Japanese): バズることより、読者に長く届く記事を作りたい。
Example 2 (English): I want to make articles with lasting reach rather than merely going viral.
Contrast: 話題になる: become a topic of conversation, broader and more neutral / 炎上する: receive concentrated negative backlash
Misuse note: Do not treat large view counts alone as proof that something バズった. The word emphasizes sudden spread and social attention.

Usage note: The fire metaphor presents criticism as rapidly spreading flames. It is not synonymous with any negative comment.
Example 1 (Japanese): 不用意な投稿が拡散され、企業アカウントが炎上した。
Example 1 (English): A careless post spread widely and triggered a backlash against the company account.
Example 2 (Japanese): 炎上後に誤情報だったと分かっても、投稿は残り続けた。
Example 2 (English): Even after the backlash was shown to rest on misinformation, the posts remained online.
Contrast: 荒れる: discussion becomes disorderly or hostile / 批判される: receive criticism, without implying viral escalation
Misuse note: Do not label ordinary disagreement 炎上 for drama. Verify the scale, concentration, and public spread of the backlash.

Usage note: In online contexts, 荒れる means discussion loses order through insults, spam, conflict, or heated repetition. The space is the grammatical subject.
Example 1 (Japanese): 最終回の解釈をめぐってコメント欄が荒れた。
Example 1 (English): The comment section turned hostile over interpretations of the finale.
Example 2 (Japanese): 台風で海が荒れている。
Example 2 (English): The sea is rough because of the typhoon.
Contrast: 炎上する: one target receives widespread backlash / 荒らされる: a space is deliberately disrupted by trolls or spam
Misuse note: Do not translate every 荒れる as an online fight. Identify whether the subject is a forum, weather, skin, lifestyle, or another condition.

Usage note: The passive 叩かれる frames the target as receiving attacks. Online, no physical hitting is implied.
Example 1 (Japanese): 発言の一部だけが切り取られ、SNSで叩かれた。
Example 1 (English): A fragment of the comment was taken out of context, and the speaker was attacked on social media.
Example 2 (Japanese): 失敗した選手を必要以上に叩くべきではない。
Example 2 (English): People should not pile on an athlete excessively for one mistake.
Contrast: 批判される: be criticized, neutral about tone / 炎上する: backlash grows into a broad public firestorm
Misuse note: Do not use 叩かれた to dismiss all criticism as abuse. Distinguish evidence-based criticism from personal attacks and coordinated harassment.

Meaning: defending camp; those supporting a target
Usage note: 擁護 means defend or speak in support, while 派 groups the supporters. The label does not state why they defend the target.
Example 1 (Japanese): 変更を評価する擁護派と、反対派で意見が分かれた。
Example 1 (English): Opinion split between those defending the change and those opposing it.
Example 2 (Japanese): 擁護派の中でも、理由は一つではない。
Example 2 (English): Even among the defenders, people have different reasons.
Contrast: 反対派: opposing camp / 支持者: supporters, often a more stable or affirmative relationship
Misuse note: Do not treat 擁護派 as a single coordinated group. It may lump together people with very different arguments.

Usage note: 界隈 avoids drawing a hard membership boundary. X界隈 can mean a fandom, professional scene, social-media cluster, or nearby social circle.
Example 1 (Japanese): そのゲーム界隈では昔から有名な話だ。
Example 1 (English): That story has long been well known in the game's community.
Example 2 (Japanese): 駅界隈には小さな飲食店が多い。
Example 2 (English): There are many small restaurants around the station.
Contrast: コミュニティ: community, often with clearer participation or structure / 業界: industry or professional field
Misuse note: Do not translate every 界隈 as 'fandom.' Check whether it means an online scene, professional circle, or literal surrounding area.

Meaning: perceived collective manners or civic conduct
Usage note: In fandom talk, 民度 usually refers to perceived collective manners: harassment, rule-following, cleanliness, or treatment of outsiders.
Example 1 (Japanese): 一部の迷惑行為だけでファン全体の民度を決めつけるのは乱暴だ。
Example 1 (English): It is unfair to judge an entire fan community by a few people's bad behavior.
Example 2 (Japanese): 民度が低いという言い方では、具体的な問題が見えにくい。
Example 2 (English): Calling the group 'low-class' hides the specific behavior that needs addressing.
Contrast: マナー: specific norms of behavior / 治安: safety or figurative orderliness of a space
Misuse note: Avoid using 民度 as if a diverse group had one moral level. Name the concrete harmful behavior instead of ranking people collectively.

Usage note: 古参 means an old or long-serving participant relative to later entrants. The relevant starting point depends on the community.
Example 1 (Japanese): 彼はデビュー当時から応援している古参ファンだ。
Example 1 (English): He is a long-time fan who has supported them since their debut.
Example 2 (Japanese): 古参だからといって、新しいファンより偉いわけではない。
Example 2 (English): Being a long-time fan does not make someone superior to newer fans.
Contrast: 新規: newcomer or recently acquired fan / 古株: long-standing member, often in a workplace or organization
Misuse note: Do not assume 古参 status proves deeper knowledge or ownership of the community. It can become a gatekeeping label.

Usage note: 新規 means new arrival, and 勢 marks a loose cohort. The term can be neutral, welcoming, self-descriptive, or gatekeeping.
Example 1 (Japanese): アニメ化をきっかけに新規勢が増えた。
Example 1 (English): The anime adaptation brought in many new fans.
Example 2 (Japanese): 新規勢にも分かる用語集を作った。
Example 2 (English): We made a glossary that newer fans can understand.
Contrast: 古参: long-time or early fan / 新規ファン: transparent, more neutral expression for a new fan
Misuse note: Do not assume new fans are less serious or knowledgeable. The label describes entry timing, not value or commitment.

Meaning: leave or move on from a fandom; graduate
Usage note: The metaphor presents leaving as completing a stage rather than failing. The object is marked with を: Xを卒業する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 受験に集中するため、しばらくアイドルオタクを卒業する。
Example 1 (English): I'm stepping away from idol fandom for a while to focus on entrance exams.
Example 2 (Japanese): 卒業したつもりだったのに、新作を見て戻ってきた。
Example 2 (English): I thought I had left the fandom, but the new release pulled me back.
Contrast: オタクをやめる: directly stop being an otaku / 担降り: stop supporting a particular favorite, especially in idol fandom
Misuse note: Do not assume fandom 卒業 is permanent, and distinguish it from a performer's officially announced graduation from a group.

Meaning: get out of a consuming hobby or fandom
Usage note: 沼 is the deep swamp of an interest; 抜け出す means manage to escape. Negative forms are especially common and often affectionate rather than regretful.
Example 1 (Japanese): グッズを減らしても、まだこの沼から抜け出せない。
Example 1 (English): Even after reducing my merchandise collection, I still cannot get out of this fandom rabbit hole.
Example 2 (Japanese): 一度沼から抜け出したのに、映画でまた戻った。
Example 2 (English): I got out of the fandom once, but the film drew me back in.
Contrast: 沼にはまる: become deeply absorbed / 卒業する: frame a deliberate departure as completing a stage
Misuse note: Avoid trivializing real compulsive spending or distress. The phrase is often playful, but context may describe a genuine need for limits.

Meaning: falling into a fandom rabbit hole
Usage note: 沼落ち compresses 'falling into the swamp' into a noun or する-verb. A trigger can be marked with 〜で or 〜をきっかけに.
Example 1 (Japanese): ライブ映像一本で、そのバンドに沼落ちした。
Example 1 (English): One concert video sent me straight down the rabbit hole for that band.
Example 2 (Japanese): 沼落ちのきっかけになった回を今でも覚えている。
Example 2 (English): I still remember the episode that drew me into the fandom.
Contrast: 沼にはまる: be or become stuck deep in the interest / ハマる: get hooked, broader and less fandom-specific
Misuse note: Do not translate 落ち as failure or romantic falling automatically. The compound means deep entry into an interest.

Meaning: more new content than fans can handle; happy overload
Usage note: 供給 is content supplied to fans; 過多 means excessive quantity. Fandom use often expresses gratitude and overwhelm at once.
Example 1 (Japanese): 新曲と配信とグッズが同日に来て、供給過多だ。
Example 1 (English): A new song, stream, and merchandise all arrived on the same day—it's a happy overload.
Example 2 (Japanese): 供給過多で、まだ昨日の動画も見終わっていない。
Example 2 (English): There is so much new content that I have not even finished yesterday's video.
Contrast: 供給不足: not enough new content / 情報過多: too much information, without the fan-content metaphor
Misuse note: Do not assume positive tone outside fandom. In economics or inventory, 供給過多 simply means excess supply.

Meaning: lack of new content; content drought
Usage note: In fan language, 供給 can include art, appearances, announcements, interactions, stories, and merchandise. The source may be official or fan-created.
Example 1 (Japanese): 半年も新情報がなくて、ファンは供給不足を感じている。
Example 1 (English): With no new information for six months, fans are feeling a content drought.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式の更新が止まり、すっかり供給不足だ。
Example 2 (English): Official updates have stopped, leaving the fandom starved for content.
Contrast: 供給過多: happy or practical overload of content / 燃料不足: humorous lack of material that sustains a theory or pairing
Misuse note: State what kind of content is missing. 供給不足 alone can sound entitled when creators are resting or under production strain.

Usage note: 限定 modifies the event's availability or eligibility. It does not inherently mean 'limited-time' unless time is the stated restriction.
Example 1 (Japanese): 購入者限定イベントの応募は今月末までだ。
Example 1 (English): Applications for the purchasers-only event close at the end of the month.
Example 2 (Japanese): その限定イベントは会員だけが参加できる。
Example 2 (English): Only members can attend that exclusive event.
Contrast: 期間限定イベント: event available only during a set period / 招待制イベント: invitation-only event
Misuse note: Do not translate 限定イベント automatically as 'limited-time event.' Determine what—time, place, audience, or quantity—is limited.

Usage note: 周年 counts complete years since an origin point; 記念 marks commemoration. It can modify a product, event, illustration, or campaign.
Example 1 (Japanese): 放送十周年記念で全話が無料配信される。
Example 1 (English): All episodes will stream free to commemorate the broadcast's tenth anniversary.
Example 2 (Japanese): 周年記念グッズの予約が始まった。
Example 2 (English): Preorders opened for the anniversary merchandise.
Contrast: 創立記念: commemoration of an organization's founding / 生誕祭: birthday celebration for a person, character, or admired figure
Misuse note: Do not omit the reference point when it could be unclear. State whether the anniversary marks publication, broadcast, debut, or founding.

Meaning: birthday celebration for a person or character
Usage note: 生誕 is a formal word for birth; 祭 turns the commemoration into an event. The celebrated subject need not attend or even be a real person.
Example 1 (Japanese): ファンが推しの生誕祭を開き、店内を写真で飾った。
Example 1 (English): Fans held a birthday celebration for their favorite and decorated the venue with photos.
Example 2 (Japanese): キャラクターの生誕祭に合わせて記念イラストが公開された。
Example 2 (English): A commemorative illustration was released for the character's birthday celebration.
Contrast: 誕生日会: ordinary birthday party / 周年記念: anniversary of a work, debut, organization, or event
Misuse note: Do not assume 生誕祭 is an official event. Fans often organize one independently, so verify organizer and authorization.

Kana: たんじょうびいらすと
Usage note: 誕生日 specifies the occasion, and イラスト the medium. Common verbs include 描く, 投稿する, and 公開する.
Example 1 (Japanese): 公式アカウントが主人公の誕生日イラストを公開した。
Example 1 (English): The official account posted a birthday illustration of the protagonist.
Example 2 (Japanese): 誕生日イラストを本人の公式タグ付きで投稿した。
Example 2 (English): I posted the birthday tribute art with the person's official hashtag.
Contrast: 記念イラスト: commemorative art for any occasion / ファンアート: fan-created art, regardless of occasion
Misuse note: Do not call an image official merely because it celebrates an official birthday. Check who created and released it.

Usage note: ファンアート identifies the creator's fan relationship, not the medium or legal status. It can be digital, traditional, sculptural, or animated.
Example 1 (Japanese): 作品のガイドラインに従ってファンアートを投稿した。
Example 1 (English): I posted fan art in accordance with the work's guidelines.
Example 2 (Japanese): 作者がファンアートを紹介しても、自由利用の許可とは限らない。
Example 2 (English): An author sharing fan art does not necessarily grant permission for unrestricted reuse.
Contrast: 公式イラスト: art released or authorized officially / 二次創作: broader derivative creation including fiction, music, video, and games
Misuse note: Do not repost, sell, or train on fan art merely because it is publicly visible. Creator rights and the source work's rights both matter.

Usage note: 感想 usually means impressions, but 感想戦 includes replaying moments, analyzing choices, and comparing interpretations—not merely stating likes and dislikes.
Example 1 (Japanese): 映画のあと、カフェで二時間も感想戦をした。
Example 1 (English): After the film, we spent two hours at a café comparing reactions and interpretations.
Example 2 (Japanese): ライブの感想戦まで含めて楽しい一日だった。
Example 2 (English): The concert and our post-show debrief made the whole day enjoyable.
Contrast: 感想会: meeting focused on sharing impressions / 反省会: review centered on mistakes and improvement
Misuse note: Do not translate 戦 literally as a fight. It is a playful extension of structured post-game review.

Usage note: 最 means most or highest; 最推し is the top choice within a person's set of 推し.
Example 1 (Japanese): 好きなキャラは多いけど、最推しは彼女だ。
Example 1 (English): I like many characters, but she is my number-one favorite.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最推しの出番は少ないが、毎週見ている。
Example 2 (English): My favorite character gets little screen time, but I still watch every week.
Contrast: 推し: a favorite one actively supports / 単推し: support focused on only one member or target
Misuse note: Do not infer exclusivity. A fan can have a 最推し and several other 推し.

Meaning: supporting the whole group; whole-group fan
Usage note: 箱推し does not always mean equal spending or identical affection toward every member. The key is supporting the collective rather than only one target.
Example 1 (Japanese): 一人に決められず、メンバー全員を箱推ししている。
Example 1 (English): I cannot choose one member, so I support the group as a whole.
Example 2 (Japanese): 最推しはいるけど、グループとしては箱推しだ。
Example 2 (English): I have a top favorite, but I support the whole group too.
Contrast: 単推し: focused support for one member / 最推し: the fan's top favorite among possible favorites
Misuse note: Do not force a binary between 箱推し and individual favorites. Fans often combine both positions.

Usage note: 神 is a slang intensifier meaning outstanding; アプデ shortens アップデート. The compound evaluates the update's effect rather than its size.
Example 1 (Japanese): 不便だった機能が全部直って、今回は神アプデだ。
Example 1 (English): This update fixed every frustrating feature; it is a fantastic patch.
Example 2 (Japanese): 神アプデと言われたが、一部の端末では不具合が出た。
Example 2 (English): Players praised it as a great update, though it caused bugs on some devices.
Contrast: 良アプデ: good update, less hyperbolic / 改悪: change judged to make a product worse
Misuse note: Do not present 神アプデ as an objective technical verdict. User groups may experience the same update differently.

Meaning: fan who supports the same favorite
Usage note: 同 means same and 担 abbreviates 担当, one's supported member in this usage. It describes overlap, not friendship or rivalry by itself.
Example 1 (Japanese): 会場で同担の人とグッズを交換した。
Example 1 (English): At the venue, I traded merchandise with someone who supports the same member.
Example 2 (Japanese): 同担歓迎なので、同じ推しの話をしたい。
Example 2 (English): I welcome fans of the same favorite and would love to talk about them.
Contrast: 他担: fan whose main favorite is someone else / 同担拒否: policy or preference to avoid fans of the same favorite
Misuse note: Do not assume all fandoms use 担当 language or that 同担 automatically means competitor. Usage is community-specific.

Meaning: preference to avoid fans of the same favorite
Usage note: 拒否 sounds strong, but practical behavior ranges from no interaction to selective avoidance. Profiles may use it to prevent conflict or jealousy.
Example 1 (Japanese): プロフィールに同担拒否と書いて、交流範囲を示している。
Example 1 (English): She states in her profile that she does not interact with fans of the same favorite.
Example 2 (Japanese): 同担拒否かどうかを相手に確認してからフォローした。
Example 2 (English): I checked whether they avoid same-favorite fans before following them.
Contrast: 同担歓迎: explicitly welcomes fans of the same favorite / 他担: fan of another member or target
Misuse note: Do not mock or pressure someone to change the boundary, but also do not use it to justify harassment or ownership claims over a person.

Meaning: our interpretations match; exactly how I see it
Usage note: 解釈 is interpretation and 一致 is agreement. As an exclamation, 解釈一致！ means 'Yes—that is exactly right for them.'
Example 1 (Japanese): その人物の優しさについては、友達と解釈一致だった。
Example 1 (English): My friend and I had exactly the same reading of the character's kindness.
Example 2 (Japanese): 新衣装が自分の想像と解釈一致でうれしい。
Example 2 (English): I'm delighted that the new outfit matches exactly how I imagined the character.
Contrast: 解釈違い: interpretations differ / 公式設定: information explicitly established by the rights holder
Misuse note: Agreement does not make an interpretation canon. Distinguish personal 解釈一致 from explicit 公式設定.

Meaning: difference in interpretation; not how I read it
Usage note: 解釈違い does not necessarily mean one side made a factual error. Many stories support more than one reading.
Example 1 (Japanese): 同じ場面でも、二人の関係について解釈違いがあった。
Example 1 (English): We interpreted the pair's relationship differently even though we watched the same scene.
Example 2 (Japanese): 解釈違いはあるけど、その絵の技術はすごいと思う。
Example 2 (English): It is not how I see the character, but the art is technically impressive.
Contrast: 解釈一致: interpretations align / 設定ミス: factual inconsistency with established setting
Misuse note: Do not use the phrase to disguise harassment of creators or other fans. A different interpretation is not automatically a mistake.

Kana: こうしききょうきゅう
Meaning: new official content or material supplied to fans
Usage note: 公式 identifies the rights holder or authorized source; 供給 frames new material as nourishment for fan interest. The phrase is appreciative and informal.
Example 1 (Japanese): 記念動画と新規イラストで、今日は公式供給が多い。
Example 1 (English): Between the anniversary video and new illustration, fans received plenty of official content today.
Example 2 (Japanese): 公式供給がなくても、過去の作品を見返して楽しんでいる。
Example 2 (English): Even without new official content, I enjoy revisiting the older material.
Contrast: ファン供給: content created or circulated by fans / 公式発表: formal official announcement, narrower and less playful
Misuse note: Do not treat every rumor, leak, or licensed resale as 公式供給. Verify that the material comes from an authorized source.
